title: A subtle swarm
caption: The dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 4789A, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4789A · constellation Coma Berenices · about 14 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The stars of NGC 4789A are smeared across the sky in a jumble with no clear order, a mix of blue and red. This dwarf irregular galaxy in the constellation Coma Berenices looks far more subtle and abstract than bright spiral or elliptical galaxies. Many more distant galaxies appear as fuzzy shapes around it.

The stars may look randomly scattered, but gravity holds them all together. Their colors have been deliberately exaggerated here to bring out the mix. The blue stars are bright, hot and massive, and they formed fairly recently. The red stars are much older. Finding both means the galaxy has been forming stars throughout its history.

Lying just over 14 million light-years from us, NGC 4789A is relatively close, which lets Hubble pick out many of its individual stars. The name fits well. A dwarf irregular galaxy is small and has no regular shape such as a spiral or an ellipse.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.18 x 1.98 arcminutes) and distance (14 million light years), the frame spans roughly 13,000 × 8,100 light-years. Its light set out about 14 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed NGC 4789A in visible and near-infrared light. The colors have been deliberately exaggerated to separate blue and red stars, and the exact mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The colors are exaggerated on purpose, so the contrast between blue and red stars is much stronger than any natural view.

explore: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded the galaxy through visible and near-infrared filters. Judy Schmidt, also known as Geckzilla, is acknowledged for the image. The fuzzy background shapes are galaxies much farther away than NGC 4789A.
alt: A loose, irregular scattering of blue and red stars with fuzzy distant galaxies in the background.
